d3768508c1.q: What is Uber for Business and what problems does it solve for enterprises?
d3768508c1.a: Uber for Business is the enterprise layer that sits on top of the consumer Uber app, helping organizations manage and optimize their mobility and meal spending. It provides a centralized platform for employees' existing personal Uber usage charged to corporate cards, offering easier expense management and giving organizations visibility and controls over how employees spend on the app.

47da13e4f4.q: How has Uber for Business structured its enablement team to balance global consistency with regional market needs?
47da13e4f4.a: Uber for Business implemented a structure combining central enablement and regional enablement. Regional enablement leads sit in-market with sales teams to respond to market-specific needs and nuances, while central enablement focuses on scalable programs like playbooks that work consistently across all regions. They communicate weekly across all regions to share best practices and identify opportunities to scale successful initiatives.

489f202a73.q: What are the key success metrics Uber for Business uses to measure AI tool adoption and impact?
489f202a73.a: Adoption is the biggest success metric, measuring how sellers are adopting and utilizing new tools. Performance metrics are also critical—they look for upticks in conversion rates or ramp time to indicate whether new tools are moving the needle and helping the business.

11652ab2b0.q: What is Uber for Business's onboarding approach for new account executives?
11652ab2b0.a: Onboarding is structured as a mix of on-demand learning and a one-week virtual live boot camp conducted via Zoom, followed by manager coaching and additional activities. A key innovation is having BDRs prospect leads before new AEs start their first day, so they arrive with warmed-up leads to accelerate their time to first opportunity and build confidence from day one.
